key_insight: In epitaxial CsPbBr3 single crystals, terahertz and Hall mobilities match quantitatively, showing that truly intrinsic charge transport can extend across millimetre-scale perovskite crystals.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical benchmark for identifying defect-free, high-mobility perovskite materials and for validating device-relevant transport measurements across length scales.
method: Concurrent optical pump-terahertz probe (OPTP) and Hall-effect measurements on the same single crystal
Temperature-dependent mobility comparison to test band-like transport
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent room-temperature mobilities of about 30 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 from both OPTP and Hall measurements, with similar temperature power laws for hole mobility.
watch_item: The result is demonstrated on high-quality epitaxial CsPbBr3 single crystals, so similar mobility matching may be harder to reproduce in polycrystalline films or defect-rich devices.
paper_title: Matching Terahertz and Hall Mobilities as a Hallmark of Intrinsic Charge Transport in Metal-Halide Perovskites
